run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T10:36:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert fires because frontend-proxy keeps emitting a small number of ERROR-status tracing spans on its 'ingress' operation: 5.21 error spans against 10120.8 spans without error status over 10:36:00-10:53:00, and the error-span rate at the alert anchor 10:36:14Z was 0.011111111111111112, exactly the value in the alert annotation; that level was already present at 10:31:14Z and non-zero earlier still. The 503s are generated inside frontend-proxy from upstream connection terminations: its access log records '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with the upstream field reading 'frontend', and the one full failing trace shows the frontend-proxy ingress span as 503 with a child client span 'router frontend egress' that received no HTTP status (http.status_code 0) and contains no frontend span at all. Identical entries occur from 10:18:19 to 10:30:23 before the alert start, so this is chronic low-level flakiness against an apparently 'above 0' threshold rather than a new onset. The frontend dependency was checked and found up: pod Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no error spans, ~123-129 MB of a 200Mi limit, ~0.052-0.056 of a 100m CPU limit, p95 span latency a stable ~295-363 ms; however ~28-37% of its CFS periods are throttled throughout the window, and the exact reason its server terminates pooled connections (for example an Envoy/frontend keep-alive idle-timeout mismatch) could not be verified because the Envoy configuration is baked into the image and the frontend container produced no log lines. A separate concurrent fault was found on fraud-detection (pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst OOMKilled, exit 137, at 10:36:16 during a recurring 'otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition' NetworkChaos run that started 10:36:13); it is not the cause of this alert because the frontend-proxy 503s predate it and neither frontend nor checkout shows any error spans.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans are confined to the 'ingress' operation: over 10:30:00-10:52:00 the increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 10.29 on span_name 'ingress' and 0 on 'router frontend egress'.

Over 10:36:00-10:53:00 the frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans increased by 5.2115 with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 10120.82 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. the error spans are a very small share of the service's spans.

At the alert anchor instant 10:36:14Z the frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0.011111111111111112 (exactly the value in the alert annotation); the same 0.011111 level was already present at 10:31:14Z and 10:32:14Z and non-zero values appear from 10:13:14Z onward, whereas the 0.018518 level appears later around 10:49-10:50.

frontend-proxy's own access log records the failing requests as '"GET ... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with the upstream field reading 'frontend', i.e. the frontend upstream terminated the connection before a response started; three such lines are at 10:36:03.493, 10:37:31.003 and 10:46:08.492 (paths /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel).

The identical '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' entries also occur before the alert start, at 10:18:19.362, 10:19:15.314, 10:19:58.804, 10:26:07.749, 10:29:35.248, 10:29:35.281 and 10:30:23.712 (seven non-2xx/3xx access-log lines in that slice), so the upstream connection resets were already happening about 18 minutes before the alert anchor.

Trace 2ba0faf4fb10d21e4381fc64c604a60a contains load-generator span 'GET' with error=true, http.status_code 503, frontend-proxy span 'ingress' with error=true, http.status_code 503, otel.status_code ERROR, and its child frontend-proxy client span 'router frontend egress' whose status tags are error="true" and http.status_code "0"; the trace has no span from the frontend service.
The frontend service emitted STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate 0 for every returned sample of the whole 09:36:14-10:53:42 window (42 samples, all zeros), i.e. no frontend error spans were observed.

Pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq are both phase Running, ready=true, restartCount 0, with no lastState termination recorded and Ready condition true since 09:57:19Z/09:57:22Z; across all 22 otel-demo pods only fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst listed restarts > 0.

The frontend container runs at ~0.043-0.056 CPU cores (limit 100m) and 122.9-128.4 MB working set (limit 200Mi) between 10:12:14 and 10:51:14, while its p95 span latency stays in the 294.9-363.2 ms band across the same period with no step at 10:36.

The frontend container is CPU-throttled for 0.28-0.37 of its CFS periods on every sample from 10:17:14 to 10:53:14 (frontend-proxy: 0.043-0.084), and the frontend-proxy container's memory working set stays ~20.2-20.7 MB against its 50Mi limit, so neither pod shows a resource spike at the alert time.

The frontend and frontend-proxy Services each resolve to exactly one ready endpoint matching the running pod (frontend -> 100.96.4.88:8080 targetRef Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t; frontend-proxy -> 100.96.4.190:8080 targetRef Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq), and both Services map port 8080 to targetPort 8080.

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst was OOMKilled (exitCode 137, finishedAt 10:36:16Z, restartCount 1, current container started 10:36:16Z) while its sibling fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b has restartCount 0; the pod's Created/Started events are stamped 10:36:16Z.

NetworkChaos events in namespace chaos-mesh show the experiment 'otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition' being applied and recovered every minute, including a run that Started at 10:36:13Z and applied chaos to otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection OOMKill and the fraud-detection/kafka NetworkChaos run at 10:36:13-10:36:16. frontend-proxy 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' lines already occur at 10:18:19-10:30:23, before that restart; the failing upstream named in those lines is 'frontend', not fraud-detection or kafka; and neither frontend nor checkout produced any STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, so no error path from that workload reaches the frontend-proxy ingress spans.

Mechanism hypothesis for the frontend-side resets: frontend-proxy's upstream HTTP connection pool reuses a keep-alive connection that the frontend HTTP server has already closed (idle-timeout or max-requests-per-connection mismatch between Envoy's 'frontend' cluster and the Next.js server), producing upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on a small fraction of requests. Neither side's timeout configuration could be read to confirm this.

Counter-evidence against frontend CPU/resource exhaustion driving the connection resets: the frontend container uses only ~0.052 of its 0.100 core limit with 122.9-128.4 MB of a 200Mi limit and an unchanged p95 latency band (~295-363 ms), and the throttling level (~0.28-0.37 of periods) is flat across the whole observed window while the 503s are intermittent.

frontend-proxy itself was not resource-starved or restarting: its container stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, at ~20.2-20.7 MB working set against a 50Mi limit and ~0.043-0.084 CFS throttling ratio, yet its ingress spans returned 503 for the upstream resets.

Read the actual Alertmanager/Prometheus definition of RequestErrorRate and consider requiring a minimum error share (not merely '> 0'), since the observed failure share is about 5.2 error spans out of about 10127 ingress spans over 17 minutes.

Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster HTTP/1 connection-pool settings (idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection) with the frontend server's keep-alive/idle timeouts, and enable or capture frontend container logs so the terminating side can be identified directly; also review the frontend CPU limit (100m) given ~28-37% CFS throttling.

Handle fraud-detection separately: its pod was OOMKilled at its 400Mi limit during the recurring 'otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition' NetworkChaos experiment, so review that memory limit and whether the chaos schedule is intended to keep running.

gaps: The alert rule itself is not readable here: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name="RequestErrorRate" returned no_data, and list_prometheus_rules with match {severity="warning"} returned no_data, so the threshold, aggregation and 'for' duration of RequestErrorRate are unknown.

The frontend-proxy span-metric series begin at 10:12:14Z (first returned sample), so there is no comparable baseline before 10:12 and whether the error rate rose relative to earlier behaviour cannot be answered.

The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration (upstream cluster timeouts and connection-pool keep-alive settings) is baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy; the only ConfigMaps returned in otel-demo are flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products, so the keep-alive/timeout hypothesis could not be verified.
The frontend container produced zero log lines for 10:36:00-10:53:42 (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data with 0 lines read), so there is no application-side evidence of why it terminated connections.
The frontend-proxy access log reads were cut by the 4 MiB read limit: lines after about 10:31:51 and after 10:47:11 were not read, so 503 entries in those spans of time are unknown.
The query for networkpolicies in otel-demo returned status no_data (count 0), so network-policy misconfiguration can be neither asserted nor excluded from this Run.

The query for PodNetworkChaos events filtered on 'frontend' returned status no_data, and NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos custom resources cannot be read with the permitted kinds; only their Kubernetes events were available, covering roughly 10:18:37-10:46:23.

Live flagd flag values are not observable from this Run; the flagd-config ConfigMap shows only static definitions with defaultVariant "off" for every flag (including loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad), so a runtime flag change cannot be excluded.
Secret values (for example DB connection strings and Kafka listener credentials referenced in Deployment env) cannot be read, so any credential-related failure is unverified.

The http_server_request_duration_seconds_count query for frontend-proxy returned no_data and only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist for that service, so request-level HTTP status shares are unknown and span counts are not request counts.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule from its rule source (Alertmanager/Prometheus rule file) to confirm its expression, threshold and evaluation window before tuning it.

Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap configuration for the 'frontend' upstream cluster (HTTP/1 connection pool idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection) and the frontend server's keep-alive timeout, then align them.

Enable or collect frontend application logs and correlate the exact 503 timestamps (10:18:19, 10:19:15, 10:19:58, 10:26:07, 10:29:35 x2, 10:30:23, 10:36:03, 10:37:31, 10:46:08) with frontend-side socket events.
Review the frontend container CPU limit (100m) and the fraud-detection memory limit (400Mi, OOMKilled at 10:36:16) with the platform team.
Review whether the recurring chaos schedule producing NetworkChaos 'otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition' every minute is intended during this period.
